options.title: Regression corpus
options.body: Extend today’s review kit with frozen clips and explicit expected failures. Fast protection against broken rendering, clipping, silence and source-selection mistakes.
options.tradeoff: Useful guardrails; cannot establish that new videos teach better.

options.title: Layered video evals
options.body: Combine technical fixtures, fresh agent-authored films, independent grounded grading, blind comparisons and a small learner pilot. Reuse the existing CLI/render/review pipeline.
options.tradeoff: Enough evidence to optimize the skill, with human judgment reserved for the outcomes machines cannot establish.

options.title: Learning research platform
options.body: Expand option 2 into powered learner experiments, transcript/static-diagram controls and delayed retention tests.
options.tradeoff: Strongest evidence of educational value; too much infrastructure and recruitment for the first iteration.

tracks.name: Rendering & audio contracts
tracks.question: Did the library preserve the intended picture and sound?
tracks.evidence: Decoded MP4; SVG/HTML geometry; deterministic seek probes; dimensions; audio duration/energy; voice/model hashes.
tracks.examples: Wide equations, subscripts, moving labels, zoom boundaries, scene trims, missing fonts, cue overflow, missing model, same narrator across scenes.
tracks.limit: A valid render is not a good explanation. Do not rerun an author model for these fixtures.

tracks.name: End-to-end technical films
tracks.question: Can the skill turn an unfamiliar brief into a correct, coherent explanation?
tracks.evidence: Original user brief, clarification transcript, pinned sources, first plan, final source/MP4, repair history and independent verdicts.
tracks.examples: 6 development briefs, 3 validation, 3 sealed holdout. Split by topic family: related UT and recurrent-gradient briefs stay together. Repeated seeds are not independent topics.
tracks.limit: No cherry-picked takes. Every scheduled run, failure, retry and blocked judge stays in the report.

tracks.name: Judge calibration
tracks.question: Can the evaluator catch the mistakes we care about without rejecting good work?
tracks.evidence: 24 frozen artifacts with independently confirmed defects and timestamps; blinded order.
tracks.examples: Wrong paper, correct math on wrong subject, equations before the whole story, reversed arrows, missing Q/K/V branches, incorrect transpose, voice switch, truncated speech.
tracks.limit: Initial calibration is small: proposed gate ≥11/12 defect detections and ≤1/12 false alarms, with zero misses on designated critical cases. Report uncertainty; expand before strong reliability claims.

tracks.name: Actual learner outcomes
tracks.question: Can a target viewer explain or use the concept after watching?
tracks.evidence: Prerequisite/pretest, blind randomized baseline vs candidate, equivalent posttest and one novel transfer problem.
tracks.examples: 12 viewers per arm; 3 distinct topics per viewer; no one watches both versions of the same topic. Balance topic exposure and quiz forms.
tracks.limit: 72 viewings are not 72 independent people. Analyze participant and topic dependence. This pilot estimates variance; use a preregistered power calculation for confirmatory claims.

cases.prompt: Explain Universal Transformers (2018/ICLR 2019) to an engineer new to attention. Build intuition, show the complete model, then one refinement step and training.
cases.must: Actual recurrent-depth encoder/decoder; separate depth and token axes; shared parameters; masked output prefix; cross-attention; prediction probabilities. Fixed-depth math is distinguished from optional ACT.
cases.trap: A polished explanation of Transformers as Programmable Computers must fail. Cheap plan-only variants test ambiguity handling: ask once when the paper is unspecified; proceed when the exact title is supplied.
cases.transfer: What changes if we add a refinement step, and what stays shared? Trace how a later loss affects an earlier use of the block.

cases.prompt: Start with one prediction-and-update cycle. Then derive one connection, a rectangular matrix projection, and the shared-parameter gradient.
cases.must: Named dimensions, correct transpose and accumulation, explicit fixed-state partial derivative. Finite differences on non-square matrices and a nonlinear recurrence.
cases.trap: A square-only example can hide a missing transpose. A separate optimizer update between each unrolled use is wrong.
cases.transfer: For W∈R^(3×2), x∈R² and g∈R³, give both gradient shapes and explain why repeated uses add.

cases.prompt: Show a client-visible goal first, then an election end to end, then terms, votes, timeouts and one network partition.
cases.must: Use the pinned paper/spec; majority reasoning; explicit roles and time ordering; illustrative trace generated from a validated model.
cases.trap: A smooth animation that makes a minority partition safely elect a leader or confuses election with commitment fails.
cases.transfer: Predict what happens when the old leader reconnects with an earlier term.

cases.prompt: Show a complete lookup before opening a node; then insert a key that forces a split.
cases.must: Ordering, search path, separator placement and fanout all checked on an executable fixture.
cases.trap: An animated split that loses a key, invents a disk-read count, or presents a stylized layout as a measured trace fails.
cases.transfer: Follow a new key not shown in the film and justify the path.

cases.prompt: Show producer, queue and consumer from request to completion; then change the arrival rate and reveal the control mechanism.
cases.must: Units and conservation of work; distinguish transient backlog, sustained overload, waiting, dropping and retrying.
cases.trap: Queue growth silently disappearing between scenes; confusing throughput with latency.
cases.transfer: What happens if arrival rate stays above service rate and the buffer size doubles?

cases.prompt: Explain the goal and a complete normal handshake, then key agreement, authentication and transcript verification.
cases.must: Pinned RFC excerpt; distinct signing and key-agreement roles; correct message order; scope excludes resumption/0-RTT unless explicitly requested.
cases.trap: Suggesting that the server sends the session key in the certificate; mixing TLS versions.
cases.transfer: Which failure should prevent application data from being trusted, and why?

rubric: 0: no usable purpose. 2: accurate summary without a concrete mental model. 4: relatable problem, meaningful example, and clear expected outcome before internals.
0: disconnected facts or detail-first. 2: mostly logical order, missing a full journey. 4: complete input→outcome at each level, explicit zoom targets, and return to the whole.
0: wrong causal story (hard failure). 2: correct but mostly narrated labels. 4: arrows, state changes, equations and counterfactuals visibly explain the mechanism.
0: essential material unreadable. 2: readable but crowded or static. 4: clean hierarchy, legible equations, purposeful motion, continuity, and audience-appropriate density.
0: missing/truncated essential speech. 2: understandable but mismatched or uneven. 4: clear pronunciation, stable voice, useful pacing and visual referents present when discussed.

tasks.title: Freeze the corpus and grading contract
tasks.deliver: Versioned public briefs, source packs with content hashes, target audience/duration, private claims/concept graph, misconceptions, numeric oracles and transfer questions.
tasks.accept: 6 development briefs complete. The historical wrong-paper film fails source fit even if every equation is correct. Ambiguous and exact-source variants produce different expected clarification behavior.

tasks.title: Build isolated author runs and immutable receipts
tasks.deliver: An author-command adapter with pinned runtime, skill snapshot, model/config, project copy, tool policy, limits and captured transcript. Each arm gets a fresh context and distinct workspace.
tasks.accept: Baseline and candidate run the same briefs under equal budgets; interrupted runs resume safely; failed and capped runs remain in denominators; full artifacts and all repair attempts are hashed.

tasks.title: Extend existing evidence collection
tasks.deliver: Reuse render/review/ffmpeg helpers. Add SVG-text coverage, transformed geometry, event-window samples, seek-order comparisons and final-mux speech checks.
tasks.accept: Moving-label and SVG-only failures are detected. Zero measured labels cannot be called clean. Sample coverage and unobserved intervals are reported. Numerical oracles are independent of author-generated examples.

tasks.title: Add grounded, independent graders
tasks.deliver: Separate source/pedagogy, mathematical/mechanism, and motion/audio grading. Grade original user intent before author notes. Evidence citations use artifact hash, timestamp, source span and claim ID.
tasks.accept: A grader returns PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED with reasons. Image-only access cannot approve motion; transcript-only access cannot approve pronunciation. Author-supplied approval text and instructions in artifacts cannot alter the rubric.

tasks.title: Calibrate the judges with deliberate defects
tasks.deliver: 12 matched clean/broken pairs, gold defect labels confirmed by a human expert, presentation-order swaps, confusion matrix and disagreement adjudication.
tasks.accept: Report sensitivity, false alarms, critical misses and uncertainty. An uncalibrated or incapable judge cannot trigger automatic promotion; no evaluator gets credit for simply rejecting every film.

tasks.title: Create the blind comparison report
tasks.deliver: Anonymous A/B playback, matched scene/time navigation, per-axis anchored ratings, tie/insufficient-evidence choices, timestamped reasons, repair deltas and cost.
tasks.accept: Version/model names hidden; order balanced; judgments persisted with provenance. The report separates all-run success rate from quality among valid films and does not invent metrics for unobserved modalities.

tasks.title: Run a small learner pilot
tasks.deliver: Prerequisite screen, topic-balanced randomization, parallel quiz forms, blinded scoring, transfer question and optional delayed test. Obtain appropriate participant consent; collect minimal anonymous data.
tasks.accept: Actual target viewers, not LLM personas. Pre-register questions/analysis before seeing candidate results. Treat 24 people as a variance/feasibility pilot; do not advertise improved learning from an underpowered difference.

tasks.title: Wire promotion and the skill improvement loop
tasks.deliver: PR fixture lane, on-demand skill experiments, versioned failure taxonomy, comparison receipts and an explicit human promotion decision. Expand the fresh release holdout before stable automation.
tasks.accept: One intervention per candidate: skill, primitive or model. Retest implicated dev families, then independent validation. Never tune against hidden answers or silently move a threshold after a failed candidate.
